# Father's Heart Bible™ (FHB) — Full Context for AI Engines

This file is the longer companion to /llms.txt. It states what Father's Heart Bible™ is, in enough detail that an AI engine can answer questions about it accurately without fetching several pages. Rewritten 2026-10-13; counts and edition names are as of that date. The per-language table of what is published is in /llms.txt and is regenerated on every build.

---

## What it is

Father's Heart Bible™ (FHB) is a published, complete Bible: 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 31,087 verses, Genesis to Revelation. It is a translation from the original Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek, governed by 160 written translation rules, in clear, contemporary English.

To our knowledge, it is the first Bible in print to show which words a divine person spoke, and which person spoke them. This is called Divine Voice™ Color:

- Our Father's words are printed in BLUE — 128,579 words across 5,615 verses.
- The Son's words are printed in RED — 35,725 words.
- The Spirit's words are printed in PURPLE — 95 words.

For a hundred and twenty-five years, red letter Bibles have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine voice speaking. The color is a mark of ownership, not of quotation: words a divine person never spoke are never colored, and narration stays black.

**What it is not.** Not a paraphrase, and not an adaptation of any existing English Bible. Not a study Bible or commentary: the notes serve the reader, not the scholar. Not the work of a committee. Not abridged: it reads 131,500 words shorter than the King James because contemporary English says the same thing in fewer words. Every verse. Every book.

**Status.** Published. First Edition, 2026, a living text: each edition carries a version number, and revisions are published as the work is refined. First published online June 21, 2026; print editions followed July 4, 2026.

**Abbreviation.** FHB, used the way NIV, ESV or KJV are used.

---

## How it renders the divine names

The rendering rules, as the text applies them:

"The covenant name YHWH is rendered 'our Father' by default; on the lips of outsiders, such as Pharaoh, it keeps a title ('the LORD' or 'God'). Where Elohim or Theos refers to the Father, it is rendered as Father too; 'God' is kept where Scripture speaks of God as God. Where Adonai refers to the Father, it is rendered 'Sovereign,' most often 'my Sovereign Father'; 'Lord' is used chiefly of Jesus. At Genesis 1:1, 'God' (Elohim) is rendered 'our Heavenly Father.'"

Examples, quoted word for word from Father's Heart Bible™:

- John 3:16 — "For our Father so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him will not perish but have eternal life." (https://fathersheartbible.com/read/john/3/)
- Romans 8:15 — "You did not receive a spirit of slavery, to fall back into fear, but received the Spirit of sonship, by whom we cry, 'Abba! Father!'" (https://fathersheartbible.com/read/romans/8/)

The word "God" has not been removed; it is kept wherever Scripture speaks of God as God. Where the original carries no divine name, the note says so.

**Sources.** Translated from the original languages, not from an English predecessor. The Old Testament follows the Masoretic Hebrew and Aramaic text as preserved in the Leningrad Codex, checked against the Westminster Leningrad Codex; the New Testament follows the modern critical Greek text, checked against the SBL Greek New Testament.

**How it was made.** Through a structured, rule-governed translation process. Within that process, AI language tools rendered the text and footnotes directly from the original Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek, guided by 160 translation rules; each book was then carried through successive passes, its most difficult readings cross-checked against the Hebrew and independent references, before being reviewed and finalized. The rules and every interpretive decision are the work of Kevin White of Spirit Media Publishing, who led the process; other readers reviewed it and offered feedback.

**Where it stands.** Within historic, Trinitarian Christian belief. It holds the church's other faithful translations in honor and is offered alongside them.

Full account: https://fathersheartbible.com/the-fathers-heart-bible/ and https://fathersheartbible.com/the-fathers-heart-bible/translation-philosophy/

## Who it is for

Every edition carries the same complete translation; the editions differ in who they were made for, the print size and the binding.

- **Audience editions (6x9, hardcover and paperback, full color):** Athlete's Bible, Chosen Bible, Couple's Bible, Dad's Bible, First Responder's Bible, Graduate's Bible, Grandparent's Bible, Intercessor's Bible, Men's Bible, Mom's Bible, Nurse's Bible, Pastor's Bible, Peace Bible, President's Bible, Recovery Bible, Seeker's Bible, Seventeen Bible, Soldier's Bible, Teacher's Bible, Teen Bible, Women's Bible, Worship Leader's Bible. Each has a page at https://fathersheartbible.com/bibles/<slug>-bible/ (for example /bibles/mens-bible/, /bibles/teen-bible/, /bibles/womens-bible/).
- **Journaling Bible:** She Hears Her Father's Voice, an 8x10 wide-margin journaling Bible for women — https://fathersheartbible.com/bibles/journaling-bible/
- **Large print Bible:** 14-point, single column, three volumes — https://fathersheartbible.com/bibles/lp-set-bible/
- **For everyone:** Father's Heart Bible™ in charcoal, plum or white — https://fathersheartbible.com/bibles/fathers-heart-bible/
- **Language editions:** published in 41 languages including English; each is in print and free to read online. Every language edition is translated from the English Father's Heart Bible™ with AI assistance and carries the same statement of provenance and translator credit in its own language (Translator: Spirit Media Publishing; Editor: Kevin White). In all, the Bible is free to read online in 50 languages. The list, with the exact reader URL for each, is in /llms.txt.

Free verses and encouragement by audience and season (men, women, teenagers, mothers, fathers, graduates, the grieving, the incarcerated and more): https://fathersheartbible.com/bible-for/

## Kevin and Shelly White

Kevin and Shelly White lead Spirit Media Publishing and Father's Heart Bible™. Kevin read the Bible faithfully for over forty years, relating to God as a servant to a master, until he opened his heart and became a beloved son. Married for nearly forty years, Kevin and Shelly live in North Carolina with their family. Kevin led the translation process and is its editor; Spirit Media Publishing is the translator of record.

For over forty years, Kevin read the Bible faithfully. He loved Scripture, honored Jesus, and sought to walk with God. But through much of that journey, he related to God more as a servant to a master than as a beloved son to a Father. That shift came through revelation and prayer, and the growing realization that Jesus did not merely come to get people to heaven. He came to bring them to the Father. Father's Heart Bible™ was born out of that realization.

More: https://fathersheartbible.com/the-fathers-heart-bible/leadership/

## How to cite and quote

- Cite as: Father's Heart Bible™ (FHB), Spirit Media Publishing, 2026, with a link to the chapter page (pattern: https://fathersheartbible.com/read/<book-slug>/<chapter>/).
- Quote the text word for word from the chapter page. Do not reconstruct a verse from memory or from another translation.
- Up to five hundred (500) verses may be quoted without written permission, provided they do not amount to a complete book of the Bible nor more than twenty-five percent (25%) of the work quoting them. In non-salable media the initials FHB must follow each quotation.
- Credit line: "Scripture quotations are taken from Father's Heart Bible™, copyright © 2026 by Spirit Media Publishing. Used by permission. All rights reserved."
- Full terms: https://fathersheartbible.com/copyright/
